title: Micro-organisms
summary: The four groups of micro-organisms, how they help and harm people, how diseases spread, and how we prevent and treat infections.

notes.text: **Micro-organisms** (microbes) are living things too small to see without a **microscope**. They are found almost everywhere: in soil, water, air, food and inside our bodies.

notes.caption: The four groups of micro-organisms
rows: The smallest; not made of cells; can only reproduce inside a living host cell
Single cells with no nucleus; reproduce quickly by splitting in two
Bacteria in yoghurt; bacteria that cause TB and cholera
Single cells with a nucleus; many live in water
Amoeba; the protist that causes malaria
Some single-celled (yeast), others form threads (moulds); feed on dead or living material
Yeast, bread mould, athlete's foot fungus

items: **Food**: yeast makes bread rise and is used to make beer; bacteria turn milk into yoghurt, cheese and amasi.
**Decomposition**: bacteria and fungi break down dead plants and animals, returning nutrients to the soil.
**Medicine**: the antibiotic penicillin comes from a mould; vaccines are made from weakened or killed microbes.
**Digestion**: bacteria in the gut help us digest food and make some vitamins.
**Sewage treatment**: bacteria break down human waste so that water can be cleaned.

notes.title: Yeast and bread
notes.problem: Explain why bread dough rises when yeast is added and the dough is left in a warm place.
steps: Yeast is a fungus that feeds on the sugar in the dough.
It respires and produces carbon dioxide gas.
Bubbles of carbon dioxide are trapped in the dough, so it swells (rises).
Warmth helps, because yeast is most active at about 25 to 35 °C.
notes.answer: Yeast produces carbon dioxide gas, which is trapped as bubbles in the dough.

notes.text: Micro-organisms that cause disease are called **pathogens** (germs). Some also spoil food: mould on bread or bacteria that make milk go sour.

notes.caption: How diseases spread
rows: Droplets in the air (coughs and sneezes)
Cover coughs, ventilate rooms, wear masks
Boil or treat water, wash hands, cook food well
Avoid contact with blood, use condoms, never share needles
Mosquito nets, insect repellent, remove standing water
Keep skin dry, do not share towels

notes.text: A substance containing weakened, dead or partial microbes that trains the immune system to recognise a pathogen, so the body can fight it quickly if infected later.
A medicine that kills bacteria or stops them from growing. Antibiotics do NOT work against viruses.

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: Always finish a full course of antibiotics. Stopping early lets the strongest bacteria survive and multiply, which leads to **antibiotic resistance**.

items: Food is preserved by keeping microbes from growing: refrigeration (cold), freezing, drying, salting, adding sugar or vinegar, canning and pasteurisation (heating milk to kill bacteria).
Personal hygiene, clean water and proper sanitation prevent many diseases.

notes.title: Breaking the chain of infection
notes.problem: A village's river is contaminated with cholera bacteria. Explain how boiling water protects people.
steps: Cholera is spread when people swallow water containing the bacteria.
Boiling water for a few minutes kills the bacteria.
With no live bacteria in the water, the chain of infection is broken.
notes.answer: Boiling kills the bacteria, so the water can no longer spread cholera.

questions.prompt: Which group of micro-organisms is the smallest and can only reproduce inside a host cell?
What is the scientific name for a micro-organism that causes disease?
Antibiotics can be used to cure flu, which is caused by a virus.
Match each example to its group.
Name the first antibiotic, which was discovered in a mould.
Explain why bread dough rises when yeast is added.
questions.memo:
✓ Yeast feeds on sugar in the dough / respires (1)
✓ It produces carbon dioxide gas (1)
✓ The gas is trapped as bubbles, making the dough expand (1)

questions.prompt: Give THREE ways in which micro-organisms are useful to people.
questions.memo:
Any three (1 each):
✓ making food (bread, yoghurt, cheese, amasi)
✓ decomposing dead material / recycling nutrients
✓ making medicines (antibiotics, vaccines)
✓ helping digestion
✓ treating sewage

questions.prompt: Why should a patient finish the whole course of antibiotics even after feeling better?
questions.memo:
✓ Some bacteria may still be alive (the strongest survive) (1)
✓ They can multiply and become resistant to the antibiotic (1)
